metadata.title: Weighted minimal surfaces in H2 x R invariant under hyperbolic translations
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we consider weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR, namely, surfaces that arise as critical points of a weighted area functional, where the corresponding weight depends only on the height function associated with the second factor R. We refer to these surfaces as {\phi}-minimal surfaces. For a class of increasing and concave weight potential functions {\phi}, we focus our attention on height-weighted minimal surfaces that are invariant under isometries of H2xR that act trivially on R and act by hyperbolic translations in H2. Through a detailed analysis of the corresponding three-dimensional system of ordinary differential equations, we present families of entire graphs, graphs over half-spaces of H2 that are asymptotic to vertical planes, winglike surfaces, and surfaces whose height function has no minimum. These families show that the hyperbolic-invariant setting is considerably richer than the rotational and parabolic settings. For the class of potential functions {\phi} we consider, they also allow us to classify all weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR that are invariant under hyperbolic translations.
